places.place_tip: See “Urban Light” at dusk for glow and lighter crowds.

places.name: Grand Central Market
places.ai_summary: Historic food hall blending classic vendors with modern eateries. Sample LA’s diversity—breakfast sandwiches, tacos, ramen, coffee, and sweets under one roof. Neon-lit evenings give it a vintage buzz.

places.name: El Pueblo de Los Angeles (Olvera Street)
places.ai_summary: Birthplace of Los Angeles with a lively Mexican marketplace, historic adobes, and cultural festivals. Handicrafts, music, and regional foods create colorful energy near Union Station—ideal for a heritage stroll and quick bites.
places.place_tip: Check holiday celebrations and folklórico schedules.

attribution.title: LosAngeles-Plaza-1869
attribution.author: Unknown authorUnknown author
attribution.description: Dating from the era of the Pueblo de Los Angeles, The Plaza and "Old Plaza Church" (Mission Nuestra Señora Reina de los Angeles) in 1869. There is a square main brick reservoir in the middle of the Plaza at the right, which was the terminus of the town's historic lifeline: the Zanja Madre. The Plaza itself was rounded and turned into a traditional ornate plaza, with a fountain that later became a bandstand. The building in the top right background was the Lugo House: first home to St. Vincent's College (now Loyola Marymount University). They are now a part of Olvera Street.

places.name: California Science Center (Exposition Park)
places.ai_summary: Hands-on science museum featuring ecosystems, aerospace, and the Space Shuttle Endeavour. Family-friendly interactives invite curiosity. Neighboring the Natural History Museum and Rose Garden for a full Exposition Park day.
places.place_tip: Time your visit for Endeavour viewing; special exhibits rotate.

places.name: Runyon Canyon Park
